commit.message:
feat(panel): a compact toggle in BOTH headers, and no title in compact mode

Three changes that belong together, because the second is what makes the first safe.

* **The panel title is dropped in compact mode.** At 176px "快捷控制" can only be drawn truncated,
  which is indistinguishable from a layout defect. The grip and the close / close-on-blur buttons
  stay: they are what makes the panel movable and closable.

* **Both headers carry a compact toggle**, and the docked one is why this exists: the double-click
  only ever reached the standalone ⚡, so dock mode had no way in at all. It is the same button in
  both — same glyph (`COMPACT_ICON_SVG`, rows of unequal length), same painted state, one painter
  (`_paintCompactToggle`) — sitting beside the close-on-blur toggle it is modelled on.

* **Each surface remembers its OWN answer** (`compactPanel` / `compactPanelDocked`). This is not
  tidiness: applying one preference to both surfaces is exactly what made the workbench panel look
  broken, because the docked panel is somebody else's window — dock-base owns its width and its
  chrome. The mode is allowed there, but it has to be ASKED, and the header button is how.

The two nodes the mode drives carry hooks (`data-dock-flash-title`, `data-dock-flash-compact-toggle`)
so section 27 can assert this on the REAL imperative head rather than at the source: the toggle is
there, the title is `display: none` while compact, pressing the button writes `compactPanel: false`
through the three-argument host call, and the title comes back with the full panel. A second sandbox
proves the independence the split exists for — `docked=true` with `floating=false` from one namespace.

270 assertions, 0 fail. dist/ rebuilt because the host schema gained the field.

@@ -263,7 +263,9 @@ Within the same group, switches are sorted by `order` ascending.
 
 ### Compact panel — double-click the ⚡
 
-Double-clicking the standalone ⚡ switches the panel to a compact form: a **narrower strip with no borders and no scrollbar, showing only each switch's icon and its control** — no labels, no descriptions, no group or tab text, and no reordering or visibility buttons. **Two consecutive toggle-only rows share one line**, so a run of them reads as a compact grid instead of a stack; a lone one keeps its half-row. It is a preference (`compactPanel`), so it follows your profile rather than the session, and double-clicking again brings the full panel back. A single click keeps its meaning — open or close — because the **second** press of a double-click is what switches the mode, so opening the panel never waits to find out whether a second click is coming.
+The mode has **two entry points**: double-click the standalone ⚡, or press the compact toggle in the panel's own header — the header button is the one that also exists in dock mode, so the docked panel can enter the mode too. It is the same button in both headers, and the two surfaces remember **their own** answer: turning it on for the floating panel never silently restyles dock-base's sidebar, and vice versa. In compact mode the panel **drops its title** — at 176px it could only be drawn truncated, which reads as a defect — while the grip and the close/close-on-blur buttons stay.
